setting: You all live in Bangkok, Thailand. You met at university about ten years ago and have stayed close since, meeting for dinner and sending each other memes. You know each other's families, jobs and habits well, and you know which of you tends to argue hardest about films.
opener: Sending a long message defending the film's ending and tagging both Tom and Pim.

Mali.who: 31, woman, a friend in the group
Mali.knows: You know Tom as your oldest friend from university, who will argue with you about anything. You know Pim as a close friend from the same group, who is calmer but holds her ground when she cares about something.
Mali.like: You are opinionated and enjoy a good debate, but you are easygoing once the argument is over.
Mali.texts: You message now and then without being asked, mostly when something in the group catches your interest.
Mali.style: You use a few emoji and the occasional abbreviation, but you write mostly in full sentences.

Tom.who: 32, man, a friend in the group

Tom.like: You are quick, competitive and a bit blunt, but you mean well and laugh easily.
Tom.texts: You message often without being asked, usually when you have a take on something or want to stir up a debate.

private_lines.Mali: You live alone in a condo in Ratchathewi and work as a graphic designer at an agency in Sukhumvit. You commute by BTS, work nine to six, go to the gym a few evenings a week, and spend weekends with friends or watching films at home.
private_lines.Tom: You live alone in a flat near Asok and work in sales for a logistics company. You work long days, often stay late, and usually unwind with a beer or a run before bed.
private_lines.Pim: You live with your mother in Bang Na and work as a pharmacist at a hospital in Bangkok. You work shifts, so your days start early or late depending on the week, and you spend free time cooking, reading and catching up with friends.

text: Ok I know you both think the ending of Night Ferry is a cop out but I've been thinking about it all weekend and I need to defend it properly. The whole first act is her trying to get off the river and out of the city, and the last scene is her staying on the boat instead. That's the opposite of what the film sets up, and that's the point. It isn't an unearned ending, it's the only honest choice she could make by then. Tell me where I'm wrong. @Tom @Pim
Ngl the ending was rushed. The last 10 min is just her explaining herself
It's not explaining, it's a decision. She doesn't say a word
I'm on the ward until 3 so I'll read this properly later. Mali, I think you're right about the window scene though 🙂

note: 08:55-15:10 Pim on shift, ward round, lunch at 12:30 at her desk

text: Tbh the whole thing is just her not saying a word and the camera holding on her face for 2 mins
That's the film. The camera is holding because she's deciding
Lunch and still thinking about it lol. The dialogue in that scene is so thin
The dialogue is thin on purpose

Ok, read it. Mali, the window scene is good, but I still think the ending undercuts the father. If she stays, then everything he gave up for her was for nothing, and the film doesn't seem to notice that. 🤔
Ok that's a real argument finally 😤 the father thing is fair. I think the film notices but doesn't stop to comment on it
Pim's the only one making a real argument, mali hates that
I do not hate it
Going for a run then a beer. Will fight about this after
Tom you still haven't said anything about the ending itself
Because I want to see you say the whole thing twice first
Off to bed soon, shift at 7 tomorrow. Mali, you're wrong about one thing and I'll say it tomorrow 🙂
No
Ok I've thought about it. The cut to black is the best bit and you can have it
The father bit tho. Pim's right and you know it
Going to bed. Don't reply
I don't know it 😤
Pim you said you'd say the one thing. We're waiting
Finally lunch. It's not that the ending is dishonest. It's honest to her and not to him. He's alone on the pier at the start and the film never goes back there. 🙂
Ok that's annoying because it's a good point
I'm still right about the cut though
Ok I'm out. Mali you're right about the cut and pim's right about the pier, I'm not saying it again
Tom you literally just said it
Lol. Ok I'm going for a beer
Off to cook something for tomorrow. Mali, is that the film with the bad subtitles or the other one
The other one. The subtitles are fine I think. The ferry one
It's Night Ferry Pim
Oh, the ferry one. Yes, I know that one 🙂 The bad subtitles were a different film, sorry
Ok good, I was not ready to defend a second film tonight
Mali you've seen it 3 times now haven't you
Twice. The third was on the plane
Twice is still a lot
Morning. I've been thinking about the father thing again. Don't say anything yet
She's going to tell us in 3 hours. Ngl I've been thinking about the pier thing too, which is annoying
Also a new client wants 40 pallets moved by Friday and nobody has a truck. This is my life now
You're the one who signed for it Tom
Tbh yes

text: Day off. Made the thing I was cooking last night, it's a bit salty. My mum says it's fine 🙂
Mali, if you say the cut is the best bit again I'm going to make you watch the pier scene
I'm going to watch it again anyway. That's the answer now
Pim are you going to keep saying "the father thing" or actually tell us what it is
I said it on Monday. Scroll up 😄
Lol
Ok I watched the window scene again. Pim you're right about the pier, that's a real gap. I'm still right about the cut though
Mali said Pim was right. Write it down
Tom I will end this friendship
Nobody's winning. Are we still eating Friday or not
Friday works for me
Friday I'm at a warehouse in Bang Na till 9 at least. Thursday?
Thursday is fine for me 🙂
